repair.proof: For f={u,v}, no u-v path avoids f or it creates a cycle. Every unique u-w tree path either avoids f or begins u-v and gives v-w suffix avoiding f; vertices cannot be reachable from both endpoints or finite-walk simplification contradicts separation. Same-side paths concatenate/simplify, yielding exactly two connected components. If f is on the tree path for non-tree edge e, endpoints of e are in opposite components. Adding e connects them and cannot create a cycle, because deleting e from such a cycle would connect opposite components in T-f. This supplies every exchange in uniqueness/necessity. For sufficiency explicitly choose an existing minimum-rank spanning tree S: if it omits any f of T, an S path crossing the cut yields a later edge to exchange out, lowering S and contradicting minimality. Hence S contains all T, and any extra edge cycles, so S=T. Finite distinct ranks/finite tree families and all tree coefficient/majorant conclusions retained.
